title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 62–71 of the 4th version of 'Analysis situs'). Grothendieck works with an abstract set M of 'pieces' (cells, strings, etc.) carrying a symmetric, antireflexive relation ‖ (disjointness / independence). The previous page builds the Galois-type closure A ↦ co-ψ°(co-ψ°(A)), where co-ψ°(A) = {X ∈ M | X ‖ Y for all Y ∈ A}. The fixed sets ('ensembles W°') form a complete lattice Σ_M with a natural orthocomplement. He also shows that a map L → M → P(L), compatible with ‖_L, induces mutually inverse isomorphisms Σ_L ⇄ Σ_M. In the 'quasi-discontinuous' case (‖_L is x ≠ y), Σ_M ≅ P(L).

This page first gives the motivation. The 'abstract' theory exists so that one can speak of immersions outside the quasi-set-theoretic case, for instance for strings ('cordes').

He then poses a representation problem. Suppose we have a faithful 'cartesian immersion' M → P(P), X ↦ |X| (defined p. 62). Can one realize Σ_M as a subset of P(P) such that:
- the order of Σ_M is induced by inclusion;
- Σ_M is stable under arbitrary sups and infs of P(P), i.e. unions and intersections;
- accessorily, |M| = P in the set-like case?
He asks: 'Est-ce toujours possible ?'

A first attempt, crossed out, sets |A|° = ∪_{X∈A} |X|° for A ⊂ M. The margin adds a doubt about whether this makes sense for general P.

The next page carries the attempt out. Take φ(X) = |X|° and assume X ‖ Y ⇔ φ(X) ∩ φ(Y) = ∅. Then A ‖ B ⇔ φ(A) ∩ φ(B) = ∅. For S = co-ψ°(A) one gets φ(S) ⊂ P∖φ(A) and X ∈ S ⇔ φ(X) ⊂ φ(S). So S ↦ φ(S) is an order embedding Σ_M → P(P). It preserves sups up to closure, and it reflects order.

In modern terms this is the closure lattice of an orthogonality space (a polarity), together with the question whether this complete ortholattice embeds as a complete sublattice of a power set.
errors: The question as posed ('Σ_M stable under arbitrary sup and inf in P(P)') generally has a negative answer, and the page does not settle it. A complete sublattice of P(P) is completely distributive. An orthocomplemented distributive lattice is Boolean, so such a realization forces Σ_M to be a complete atomic Boolean algebra. Even when ‖ is induced by disjointness of subsets of P, Σ_M can fail to be distributive. Example: P = {1,2,3,4}, M = {{1,2},{2,3},{3,4},{4,1}} with disjointness. The orthoclosed sets are ∅, the four singletons and M, which gives the non-distributive lattice MO2. Under φ, the meet {X}∧{Y} = ∅ maps to ∅, but φ{X} ∩ φ{Y} = {2}. So inf-stability fails. Grothendieck's own margin doubt ('cela fait-il sens ... général!') is justified. The next page's construction only gives an order embedding with the sup-side property, not inf-stability.

ideas.what: The lattice Σ_M of sets closed under double orthogonality for a symmetric antireflexive 'disjointness' relation on a set of pieces
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space / polarity and its complete ortholattice of orthoclosed subsets (Galois closure)

ideas.what: Representing the abstract lattice Σ_M inside P(P) via a faithful 'cartesian immersion' X ↦ |X|, with induced order and stability under arbitrary unions and intersections
ideas.modern_name: Representation of a complete lattice as a complete sublattice of a power set (possible only for completely distributive / atomic Boolean cases)

ideas.what: Motivation: an abstract, non-set-theoretic theory of 'immersions' of cell-like pieces, so as to handle strings (cordes) etc.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial / tame-topology formalism for supports and immersions
ideas.where_published: Possibly related in spirit to the 'topologie modérée' programme in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's abstract analysis situs uses exactly the structure of an orthogonality space and its ortholattice of closed sets, a structure central to quantum logic (Foulis–Randall, Dacey). He does this in a purely topological–combinatorial context (supports of cells and strings) and asks when this ortholattice is realized by honest point sets. The answer is when it is Boolean, as in the 'quasi-discontinuous' case.
missed.quote: j'ai envie alors de définir une réalisation Σ_M ⊂ P(P) de telle façon que la relation d'ordre de Σ_M soit induite par celle de P(P), que Σ_M soit stable par sup et inf quelconques ... Est-ce toujours possible ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a mild curiosity: an independent rediscovery of orthogonality-space closure in a topological setting. The non-distributive cases would correspond to 'non-pointlike' configurations, e.g. strings. Not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a motivational remark plus an open representation question that is elementary and has a known (generally negative) answer. The only interest is the unpublished framework of abstract 'immersions' with a disjointness relation, which coincides with orthogonality spaces.
transcription_corrections: Line 6–7: should read 'Supposons qu'on ait une partition / immersion cartésienne fidèle'. 'immersion' is written above/over 'partition' as a correction, not as an unreadable word.
The struck-out text after 'une' reads 'application injective, avec' and 'réalisation' is inserted above it; this is consistent with the transcription.
The left marginal note runs diagonally and seems to read roughly 'mais cela fait-il bien sens ... P ... général !'. The words are uncertain, but the gist is a doubt about generality.
The crossed-out final block ends with 'Donc si A, B ⊂ M, on a A ∩ ...', which matches the image (struck through with diagonal lines).
